title: The density paradox: density, walking, and psychological stress in overcrowded public spaces
limitations: Non-empirical review; no original research findings reported
Lack of consensus on how physical density was defined and measured in previous studies
Multiple, non-uniform definitions for psychological stress across disciplines
Uncertainty about particular density thresholds affecting walking and psychological stress
Speculative nature of answers to core research questions due to lack of science-based knowledge
Limited understanding of cultural and normative differences in density perception across populations
overall_theory_links: Physical density as built environment attribute with dual effects: promotes walking (physical activity) but may increase psychological stress (mental health burden)
Social density (unique social encounters per unit time) as potentially modifiable trigger for psychological stress
Non-linear relationship between population density and walking behavior (benefits attenuate after threshold)
Perception of density varies by individual norms, culture, and ideal interaction levels; high physical density does not necessarily lead to crowding
Environmental cues (lights, noise, temperature, green spaces, stranger presence) influence people's evaluation of physical density
filename_mismatch: File labeled as Kimmel paper but contains Koohsari et al. (2024) paper on density paradox
